articleTitle: Correlation-immunity of nonlinear combining functions for cryptographic applications (Corresp.)
abstract: Pseudonoise generators for cryptographic applications consisting of several linear feedback shift registers with a nonlinear combining function have been proposed as running key generators in stream ciphers. These running key generators eau sometimes be broken by (ciphertext-only) correlation attacks on individual subsequences. A new class of combining functions is presented, which provides better security against such attacks. The security is quantified by the smallest number<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m + 1</tex>of subsequences that must be simultaneously considered in a correlation attack. A necessary condition for such<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</tex>th-order correlation-immunity is proved. A recursive construction is given that permits the construction of an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</tex>th-order immune combining function for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>subsequences for any<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>with<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1 \leq m < n</tex>. Finally, the trade-off between the length of the linear equivalent of the nonlinear generator and the order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</tex>of its immunity against correlation attacks is considered.

articleTitle: The capacity of the white Gaussian multiple access channel with feedback
abstract: Since the appearance of [10] by Gaarder and Wolf, it has been well known that feedback can enlarge the capacity region of the multiple access channel. In this paper a deterministic feedback code is presented for the two-user Gaussian multiple access channel, which is shown to allow reliable communication at all points inside a region larger than any previously obtained. An outer bound is given which is shown to coincide with the achievable region, thus yielding the capacity region of this channel exactly.

articleTitle: Some complexity results about packet radio networks (Corresp.)
abstract: It is shown that the decision problem regarding the membership of a point in the capacity region of a packet radio network is nondeterministic polynomial time hard (NP hard). The capacity region is the set of all feasible origin-to-destination message rates where feasibility is defined as the existence of any set of rules for moving the data through the network so that the desired rates are satisfied.

articleTitle: Nonbinary codes, correcting single deletion or insertion (Corresp.)
abstract: In many digital communications systems, bursts of insertions or deletions are typical errors. A new class of nonbinary codes is proposed that correct a single deletion or insertion. Asymptotically, the cardinality of these codes is close to optimal. The codes can be easily implemented.

articleTitle: GMW sequences (Corresp.)
abstract: The difference set design of Gordon, Mills, and Welch (GMW) is adapted for use as a pseudorandom number generator. Statistical properties of the generated binary sequences, including periodic correlation, linear span, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</tex>-tuple statistics, are derived. One mechanization of a GMW sequence generator is suggested, and the number of sequences that can be generated with a fixed number of shift-register stages and read-only memory (ROM) size is evaluated.

articleTitle: An achievable region and outer bound for the Gaussian broadcast channel with feedback (Corresp.)
abstract: A deterministic coding scheme is presented for additive white Gaussian broadcast channels with two receivers and feedback from the receivers to the transmitter. The region of data rates at which reliable communication is possible is larger than that of the corresponding channel without feedback. This is the first example showing that the capacity region of degraded broadcast channels can be enlarged with feedback.

articleTitle: A polynomial-time algorithm for breaking the basic Merkle - Hellman cryptosystem
abstract: The Merkle-Hellman cryptosystem is one of the two major public-key cryptosystems proposed so far. It is shown that the basic variant of this cryptosystem, in which the elements of the public key are modular multiples of a superincreasing sequence, is breakable in polynomial time.

articleTitle: An algorithm for maximizing expected log investment return
abstract: Let the random (stock market) vector<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X \geq 0</tex>be drawn according to a known distribution function<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F(x), x \in R^{m}</tex>. A log-optimal portfolio<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b^{\ast}</tex>is any portfolio<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</tex>achieving maximal expected<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\log</tex>return<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">W^{\ast}=\sup_{b} E \ln b^{t}X</tex>, where the supremum is over the simplex<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b \geq 0, \sum_{i=1}^{m} b_{i} = 1</tex>. An algorithm is presented for finding<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b^{\ast}</tex>. The algorithm consists of replacing the portfolio<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</tex>by the expected portfolio<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b^{'}, b_{i}^{'} = E(b_{i}X_{i}/b^{t}X)</tex>, corresponding to the expected proportion of holdings in each stock after one market period. The improvement in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">W(b)</tex>after each iteration is lower-bounded by the Kullback-Leibler information number<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D(b^{'}\|b)</tex>between the current and updated portfolios. Thus the algorithm monotonically improves the return<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">W</tex>. An upper bound on<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">W^{\ast}</tex>is given in terms of the current portfolio and the gradient, and the convergence of the algorithm is established.

articleTitle: Codes for zero spectral density at zero frequency (Corresp.)
abstract: In pulse-amplitude modulation (PAM) digital transmission systems line encoding is used for shaping the spectrum of the encoded symbol sequence to suit the frequency characteristics of the transmission channel. In particular, it is often required that the encoded symbol sequence have a zero mean and spectral density vanishing at zero frequency. We show that the finite running digital sum condition is a necessary and sufficient condition for this to occur. The result holds in particular for alphabetic codes, which are the most widely used line codes.

articleTitle: Duadic Codes
abstract: A new family of binary cyclic<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(n,(n + 1)/2)</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(n,(n - 1)/2)</tex>codes are introduced, which include quadratic residue (QR) codes when<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>is prime. These codes are defined in terms of their idempotent generators, and they exist for all odd<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n = p_{1}^{a_{1}} p_{2}^{a_{2}} \cdots p_{r}^{a_{r}}</tex>where each<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p_{i}</tex>is a prime<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\equiv \pm 1 \pmod{8}</tex>. Dual codes are identified. The minimum odd weight of a duadic<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(n,(n + 1)/2)</tex>code satisfies a square root bound. When equality holds in the sharper form of this bound, vectors of minimum weight hold a projective plane. The unique projective plane of order 8 is held by the minimum weight vectors in two inequivalent<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(73,37,9)</tex>duadic codes. All duadic codes of length less than<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">127</tex>are identified, and the minimum weights of their extensions are given. One of the duadic codes of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">113</tex>has greater minimum weight than the QR code of that length.

articleTitle: Algorithms for the generation of full-length shift- register sequences
abstract: Two algorithms are presented for the generation of full-length shift-register cycles, also referred to as de Bruijn sequences. The first algorithm generates<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2^{k \cdot g(n,k)</tex>full cycles of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2^{n}</tex>, using<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3n + k \cdot g(n, k)</tex>bits of storage, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</tex>is a free parameter in the range<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1 \leq k \leq 2^{((n-4)/2)}</tex>, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g(n, k)</tex>is of the order of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n - 2 \log k</tex>. The second algorithm generates about<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2^{n^{2}/4}</tex>full cycles of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2^{n}</tex>, using about<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n^{2}/2</tex>bits of storage. In both algorithms, the time required to produce the next bit from the last<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>bits is close to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>. A possible application to the construction of stream ciphers is indicated.

articleTitle: Weak convergence and asymptotic properties of adaptive filters with constant gains
abstract: The basic adaptive filtering algorithm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X_{n+1}^{\epsilon} = X_{n}^{\epsilon} - \epsilon Y_{n}(Y_{n}^{'}X_{n}^{\epsilon} - \psi_{n})</tex>is analyzed using the theory of weak convergence. Apart from some very special cases, the analysis is hard when done for each fixed<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\epsilon > 0</tex>. But the weak convergence techniques are set up to provide much information for small<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\epsilon</tex>. The relevant facts from the theory are given. Define<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x^{\epsilon}(\cdot)</tex>by<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x^{\epsilon}(t) = X_{n}^{\epsilon}</tex>on<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[n\epsilon, n\epsilon + \epsilon)</tex>. Then weak (distributional) convergence of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\{x^{\epsilon}(\cdot)\}</tex>and of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\{x^{\epsilon}(\cdot + t_{\epsilon})\}</tex>is proved under very weak assumptions, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t_{\epsilon} \rightarrow \infty</tex>as<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\epsilon \rightarrow 0</tex>. The normalized errors<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\{(X_{n}^{\epsilon} - \theta ) / \sqrt{\epsilon} \}</tex>are analyzed, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\theta</tex>is a "stable" point for the "mean" algorithm. The asymptotic properties of a projection algorithm are developed, where the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X_{n}^{\epsilon}</tex>are truncated at each iteration, if they fall outside of a given set.

articleTitle: On the similarity of the entropy power inequality and the Brunn- Minkowski inequality (Corresp.)
abstract: The entropy power inequality states that the effective variance (entropy power) of the sum of two independent random variables is greater than the sum of their effective variances. The Brunn-Minkowski inequality states that the effective radius of the set sum of two sets is greater than the sum of their effective radii. Both these inequalities are recast in a form that enhances their similarity. In spite of this similarity, there is as yet no common proof of the inequalities. Nevertheless, their intriguing similarity suggests that new results relating to entropies from known results in geometry and vice versa may be found. Two applications of this reasoning are presented. First, an isoperimetric inequality for entropy is proved that shows that the spherical normal distribution minimizes the trace of the Fisher information matrix given an entropy constraint--just as a sphere minimizes the surface area given a volume constraint. Second, a theorem involving the effective radii of growing convex sets is proved.

articleTitle: An improved algorithm for evaluating trellis phase codes (Corresp.)
abstract: A method is described for evaluating the minimum distance parameters of trellis-phase codes, including continuous phase frequency shift keying (CPFSK), partial-response FM, and, more importantly, coded continuous-phase modulation (CPM) schemes. The algorithm provides dramatically faster execution times and smaller memory requirements than previous algorithms. Results of sample calculations and timing comparisons are included.

articleTitle: Packings ofR^nby certain error spheres
abstract: Golomb in 1969 defined error metrics for codes and their corresponding "error spheres." Among the error spheres are the cross and semicross. The cross is defined as follows. Let<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>be positive integers. The<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(k, n)</tex>-cross in Euclidean<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>-space<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R^{n}</tex>consists of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2kn + 1</tex>unit cubes: a central cube together with<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n</tex>arms of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</tex>. The<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(k, n)</tex>-semicross in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R^{n}</tex>consists of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">kn + 1</tex>unit cubes: a comer cube together with<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>arms of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</tex>attached at<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>of its nonopposite faces. For instance, the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1, 2)</tex>-cross has five squares arranged in a cross and the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1, 2)</tex>-semicross is shaped like the letter<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</tex>. Much has been done on determining when translates of a cross or semicross tile (or tesselate)<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R^{n}</tex>. If translates do not tile, we may ask how densely they can pack space without overlapping. We answer this question for the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(k, n)</tex>-cross in all dimensions and for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</tex>large. We also show that packings by the cross that are extremely regular (lattice packings) do just about as well as arbitrary packings by the cross. However, for the semicross, even in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R^{3}</tex>, when the arm length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</tex>is large, lattice packings are much less dense than arbitrary packings. The methods are primarily algebraic, involving Abelian groups.

articleTitle: An upper bound on the aperiodic autocorrelation function for a maximal-length sequence (Corresp.)
abstract: The magnitude of the out-of-phase aperiodic autocorrelation function for a maximal-length linear feedback shift register sequence of period<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</tex>is at most<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1 + (2/ \pi)(N + 1)^{1/2} \ln(4N/ \pi)</tex>. Previously, the best upper bound was<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(N + 1)^{1/2} \ln (eN)</tex>.

articleTitle: Construction of de Bruijn sequences of minimal complexity
abstract: It is well known that the linear complexity of a de Bruijn sequence<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</tex>of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2^{n}</tex>is bounded below by<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2^{n- 1} + n</tex>for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n \geq 3</tex>. It is shown that this lower bound is attainable for all<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>.

articleTitle: Distribution-free consistency of a nonparametric kernel regression estimate and classification
abstract: It is shown that the kernel estimate of the regression<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E(Y|X = x)</tex>is weakly or strongly consistent for almost all<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x(\mu)</tex>, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\mu</tex>is the probability measure of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</tex>. The result is valid for any distribution of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</tex>. The asymptotical optimality of classification rules derived from the estimate is examined. The optimality is independent of class distributions, i.e., it is distribution-free.

articleTitle: Modular curves and codes with a polynomial construction
abstract: In this paper we study<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</tex>-ary codes arising from modular curves<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X_{0}(11l)</tex>over GF<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(p^{2})</tex>and some binary codes attached to them. All these codes have a polynomial construction and have "good" asymptotic parameters: for certain values of the parameters the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</tex>-ary codes with<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q = p^{2} \geq 49</tex>are better than the Varshamov-Gilbert bound, and the binary codes are better than the Ziablov bounds.

articleTitle: Characterizing the radar ambiguity functions
abstract: Ambiguity functions are expanded relative to cross-ambiguity functions associated with a special orthonormal basis of signal space related to a rectangular pulse. The cross-ambiguity functions are simply related to the well-known ambiguity function of a rectangular pulse. The description of ambiguity functions in terms of these well-known and interrelated cross-ambiguity functions facilitates the ease with which desired calculations can be made. Indeed, one can compute the ambiguity function of a signal as easily as taking the Fourier series of a periodic function. The characterization of ambiguity functions resulting from this expansion is applied to prove two general results about the set of all ambiguity functions. We prove that the set of ambiguity functions is closed on the square-integrable topology and that, except in a trivial case, the sum of two ambiguity functions is never an ambiguity function.

articleTitle: Optimum cyclic redundancy codes for noisy channels (Corresp.)
abstract: Binary cyclic redundancy codes for feedback communication over noisy digital links are considered. The standard 16-bit ADCCPt polynomial is designed for digital links that already have a low input bit error probability. For file transfer between personal computers over telephone circuits, the quality of the resulting digital circuit may be much lower. This leads to the consideration of 3-byte (24-bit) and 4-byte (32-bit) polynomials. Generator polynomials of a certain class are found that have minimum weight and yet achieve the bound on minimum distance for arbitrary codes. Particular polynomials for 24-bit and 32-bit redundancies are exhibited, of weight and distance 6 in the 24-bit case and weight 10 and distance 8 in the 32-bit case.

articleTitle: Maxentropic Markov chains (Corresp.)
abstract: The Markov chain that has maximum entropy for given first and second moments is determined. The solution provides a discrete analog to the continuous Gauss-Markov process.

articleTitle: The complexity of computing the covering radius of a code
abstract: The problem of finding the covering radius of a binary linear code is shown to be nondeterministic polynomial (NP)-hard. In fact, a problem that is complete for the class<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\prod_{2}^{p}</tex>in the polynomial hierarchy is shown to be reducible to the covering-radius problem, so that finding the covering radius is strictly harder than any NP-complete problem unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses with NP =<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\prod_{2}^{p}</tex>.

articleTitle: Linear unequal error protection codes from shorter codes (Corresp.)
abstract: The methods for combining codes, such as the direct sum, direct product, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">|u|u + v|</tex>constructions, concatenation, etc., are extended to linear unequal error protection codes.

articleTitle: Further results on coding for T-user multiple-access channels (Corresp.)
abstract: Coding schemes for the noiseless<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</tex>-user binary adder multiple-access channel are discussed. A class of uniquely decodable codes of arbitrary length satisfying a specific recursive relationship and which are asymptotically good is explicitly constructed.

articleTitle: Almost everywhere convergence of a recursive regression function estimate and classification (Corresp.)
abstract: It is shown that the recursive kernel estimate of the regression function<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E(Y|X = x)</tex>is consistent at almost every<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x(\mu)</tex>regardless of the distribution<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\mu</tex>of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</tex>. Thus the result is distribution-free. From this we show that the risk for a suitable classification rule derived from the estimate converges to Bayes' risk, no matter what the class distributions are.

articleTitle: Two results on the asymptotic performance of quantizers
abstract: A necessary and sufficient condition is presented for the normalized asymptotic<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</tex>th power distortion of a mismatched multidimensional quantizer to converge to a certain optimum constant known as Bennett's integral. The dimensionality of our results is allowed to approach infinity in order to make some universal source coding comparisons to quantization theory.

articleTitle: Fixed-rate encoding of individual sequences with side information
abstract: For every infinite sequence<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</tex>and a given side-information sequence<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</tex>, we define a quality<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H(x|y)</tex>called the finite-state conditional complexity of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</tex>given<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</tex>. It is shown that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H(x|y)</tex>is the smallest asymptotically attainable fixed-rate at which<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</tex>can be transmitted with negligibly small distortion, given<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</tex>. Moreover, it is demonstrated that in order to achieve an arbitrary small distortion for all sequences such that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H(x|y)</tex>is less than the allowable transmission rate it is not necessary for the encoder to have access to the side-information sequence<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</tex>(provided it is available to the decoder). This result is a generalization of the classical Slepian-Wolf result for cases where the probabilistic characterization of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</tex>is not known, or does not exist.

articleTitle: On the minimum distance of some quadratic residue codes (Corresp.)
abstract: We find the minimum distances of the binary<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(113, 57)</tex>, and ternary<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(37, 19), (61, 31), (71, 36)</tex>, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(73, 37)</tex>quadratic residue codes and the corresponding extended codes. These distances are<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15, 10, 11, 17</tex>, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</tex>, respectively, for the nonextended codes and are increased by one for the respective extended codes. We also characterize the minimum weight codewords for the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(113, 57)</tex>binary code and its extended counterpart.

articleTitle: A new linear convex hull algorithm for simple polygons (Corresp.)
abstract: A new optimal algorithm for computing the convex hull of a simple polygon in the plane, along with a proof of correctness, is presented. The main novelty of the proposed algorithm is its use of existing concepts such as the unimodality of the area of a triangle inscribed in a convex polygon and Sldansky's scan. The combination of these concepts gives us new insight into the problem.

articleTitle: Modified product codes
abstract: By modifying product codes, a new coding scheme and its decoding method are proposed. Compared to a product code<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</tex>, the first stage code<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A_{1}</tex>of the new code<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A_{M}</tex>is constructed in the same way as that of the code<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</tex>except that it has at least one subcode, while the second stage codes<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A_{2}^{(j)}</tex>of the code<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A_{M}</tex>are a set of codes With the same length and different rates. The new coding scheme has a smaller upper bound on the probability of decoding error than the original product coding scheme for any given nonzero rate less than the capacity of a binary symmetric channel. An example is given for which the rate is increased compared With the original product code, at a fixed probability of decoding error, for a relatively short code length.

articleTitle: Adaptive linear procedures under general conditions
abstract: Under mild conditions on the observation processes the almost sure convergence properties of linear stochastic approximation are summarized for least squares and for some of its applications: adaptive filtering, echo cancellation, detection of binary data in Gaussian noise, identification, and linear classification.

articleTitle: On the distribution of de Bruijn sequences of given complexity
abstract: The distribution<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\gamma (c, n)</tex>of de Bruijn sequences of order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>and linear complexity<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</tex>is investigated. It is shown that for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n \geq 4, \gamma (2^{n} - 1, n) \equiv 0 \pmod{8}</tex>, and for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k \geq 3, \gamma (2^{2k} - 1,2k) \equiv 0 \pmod{l6}</tex>. It is also shown that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\gamma (c, n) \equiv 0 \pmod{4}</tex>for all<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</tex>, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n \geq 3</tex>such that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cn</tex>is even.

articleTitle: Combinatorial packings ofR^3by certain error spheres
abstract: This paper concerns one of the "error spheres" discussed by Golomb in 1969, his "Stein corner" in three-dimensional Euclidean space<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R^{3}</tex>. This figure, which we shall call a semicross, is defined as follows. Let<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</tex>be a positive integer. The<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(k, 3)</tex>-semicross consists of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3k + 1</tex>unit cubes: a corner cube together with three nonopposite arms of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</tex>. (It may be thought of as a tripod.) For<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k \geq 2</tex>translates of the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(k, 3)</tex>-semicross do not tile<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R^{3}</tex>. The question of how densely the translates pack<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R^{3}</tex>will be examined by combinatorial techniques. While the maximum density is not determined, sufficiently dense packings are produced to show that they are much denser than the densest lattice packing.

articleTitle: On the continued fraction and Berlekamp's algorithm (Corresp.)
abstract: Continued fraction techniques are equivalent to Berlekamp's algorithm. The sequence<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D(k), k \geq 0</tex>, in Berlekamp's algorithm provides the information about when Berlekamp's algorithm completes one iterative step of the continued fraction. In fact, this happens when<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D(K) < k + 1/2</tex>; and when<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D(k) \neq D(k + 1)</tex>, it implies that Berlekamp's algorithm begins the next iterative step of the continued fraction.

articleTitle: On the p-point uncertainty class (Corresp.)
abstract: The<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</tex>-point uncertainty class (also known as Sakrison's class b) is considered. Although the p-point class is not a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</tex>-alternating Choquet capacity class, it is shown how many of the robust signal processing and communication theory results which have been developed for capacity classes can be applied to the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</tex>-point class by embedding it in a slightly larger "extended<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</tex>-point class."

articleTitle: ARMA spectral estimation of time series with missing observations
abstract: The problem of estimating the power spectral density of stationary time series when the measurements are not contiguous is considered. A new autoregressive moving-average (ARMA) method is proposed for this problem, based on nonlinear optimization of a weighted-squared-error criterion. The method can handle either regularly or randomly missing observations. As a special case, the method can handle the problem of missing sample covariances. The computational complexity is modest compared to exact maximum likelihood estimation of the same parameters. The performance of the algorithm is illustrated by some numerical examples and is shown to be statistically efficient in these cases.

articleTitle: A note on binary arrays with a certain window property (Corresp.)
abstract: For some<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rs = 2^{mn}</tex>, there exist periodic<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r \times s</tex>binary arrays such that all<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m \times n</tex>binary matrices will appear in it. As two-dimensional versions of de Bruijn sequences, these kinds of arrays have possible applications in cryptography and the design of mask configurations for spectrometers.

articleTitle: A method for extending binary linear codes (Corresp.)
abstract: Five binary linear<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[n, k, d]</tex>codes are presented that contain more words than the codes with corresponding values of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</tex>that are listed in the table of MacWilliams and Sloane. The construction method is a generalization of Construction<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</tex>of Sioane, Reddy, and Chen.

articleTitle: Maximum distance separable multilevel codes (Corresp.)
abstract: A class of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</tex>error-correcting pseudocyclic multilevel codes is introduced. These are maximum-distance separable random-error-correcting codes with qm symbols, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</tex>is a prime number. The construction of seven-level codes is presented as an example.

articleTitle: On a relation between maximum likelihood classification and minimum relative-entropy classification (Corresp.)
abstract: Maximum likelihood (ML) and minimum relative-entropy (MRE) (minimum cross-entropy) classification of samples from an unknown probability density when the hypotheses comprise an exponential family are considered. It is shown that ML and MRE lead to the same classification nde, and the result is illustrated in terms of a method for estimating covariance matrices recently developed by Burg, Luenberger, and Wenger, MRE classification applies to the general case in which it cannot be assumed that the samples were generated by one of the hypothesis densities. The common use of ML in this case is technically incorrect, but the equivalence of MRE and ML provides a theoretical justification.

articleTitle: Monotony of Lloyd's method II for log-concave density and convex error weighting function (Corresp.)
abstract: Kieffer recently showed that for a log-concave probability density there is a unique<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</tex>-level quantizer which is a stationary point of the expected value of an increasing, convex, and continuously differentiable error weighting function, dependent on the absolute quantization error. It is shown that the requirement of continuous differentiability can be dropped, using the monotony of Lloyd's Method II, the proof of which is based on a generalization of previous work by the author.

articleTitle: A [55,16,19] binary Goppa code (Corresp.)
abstract: A<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[55, 16, 19]</tex>binary Goppa code and some related codes are described. These codes are found to contain more codewords than any previously known codes of the same length and minimum distance.

articleTitle: Asymptotic memoryless discrete-time detection ofphi-mixing signals inphi-mixing noise (Corresp.)
abstract: In this correspondence we consider the design of memoryless discrete-time detectors for a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\phi</tex>-mixing signal in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\phi</tex>-mixing noise, where a large degree of dependency may exist between the signal and the noise. The fidelity criterion is taken to be the asymptotic relative efficiency, and it is shown that with this fidelity criterion the nonlinearity in the optimal detector can be found as the solution of an integral equation in which knowledge of only the second-order statistics of the random processes involved is required.

articleTitle: A note on extended quadratic residue codes overGF(9)and their ternary images (Corresp.)
abstract: We discuss<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2(p + 1), p + 1]</tex>double circulant codes which are the ternary images of the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[p + 1,(p + 1)/2]</tex>extended quadratic residue codes over GF<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(9)</tex>. Here<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</tex>is a prime of the form<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p = 12k \pm 5</tex>. As a special result we obtain a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[64, 32,18]</tex>ternary self-dual code which is the largest known code meeting the bound of Mallows and Sloane.

articleTitle: On multiple access channels with feedback (Corresp.)
abstract: For the binary erasure multiple access channel, van der Meulen showed in his survey paper that the symmetrical rate pair<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(0.79113,0.79113)</tex>is achievable in the ease of feedback. Here we prove that this rate point is on the boundary of the feedback capacity region. Subsequently we apply this result to demonstrate the fact that the feedback capacity region of the product of two multiple access channels can be strictly larger than the (Minkowski)sum Of the feedback capacity regions for the separate channels.

articleTitle: A polynomial form for logarithms modulo a prime (Corresp.)
abstract: An explicit polynomial form for logarithm functions modulo a prime p is given; the coefficients have a surprisingly simple form. It follows that any polynomial that represents a logarithm modulo<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</tex>has at least<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p - 2</tex>nonzero coefficients and is therefore highly inefficient to use as a computational method.

articleTitle: Improved maximum-likelihood detection and estimation of Bernoulli - Gaussian processes (Corresp.)
abstract: When a wavelet to be estimated is not spiky, then a single most likely replacement (SMLR) detector, which is used to detect randomly located impulsive events that have Gaussian-distributed amplitudes, may split a large spike into two smaller ones and may also detect some spikes at wrong locations, although these locations are very close to their true ones. Presented here are two new detection algorithms, namely a single-spike-shift (SSS) detector and an SSS-SMLR detector both of which help correct the SMLR detector's spike-splitting and shifting problem.

articleTitle: A generalization of the near-optimum binary coherent state receiver concept (Corresp.)
abstract: The structure of a maximum {\em a posteriori} decoder is derived for binary optical fields processed according to Kennedy's near-optimum scheme, but operating in the presence of random optical phase-error and interfering background fields. An exact expression is found for the error probability, and examples to illustrate decoder performance under various operating conditions of interest are provided.

articleTitle: A product construction for perfect codes over arbitrary alphabets (Corresp.)
abstract: A general product construction for perfect single-error-correcting codes over an arbitrary alphabet is presented. Given perfect single-error-correcting codes of lengths<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n, m</tex>, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q + 1</tex>over an alphabet of order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</tex>, one can construct perfect single-error-correcting codes of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(q - 1)nm + n + m</tex>over the same alphabet. Moreover, if there exists a perfect single-error-correcting code of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q + 1</tex>over an alphabet of order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</tex>, then there exist perfect single-error-correcting codes of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n = (q^{t} _ 1)/(q - 1)</tex>, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(t > 0</tex>, an integer). Finally, connections between projective planes of order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</tex>and perfect codes of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q + 1</tex>over an alphabet of order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</tex>are discussed.

articleTitle: A min-max theorem for antijamming group codes
abstract: Slepian's idea of group codes for analog channels is adapted to the case of antijamming codes. The main result is a codeword error probability characterized by a min-max theorem. The result is illustrated by the special cases of frequency hopping (FH) and direct sequence (DS).

articleTitle: An approach to an arithmetic analog of Berlekamp's algorithm (Corresp.)
abstract: The Berlekamp algorithm used for generating convergents (polynomial fractions) to a polynomial sequence is altered for use with binary numbers. This provides an alternative to continued fraction generation of convergents, and the proposed algorithm uses no division. However optimality has not been proved unlike the case for the Berlekamp algorithm with polynomial sequences.

articleTitle: A new upper bound on the first-event error probability for maximum-likelihood decoding of fixed binary convolutional codes (Corresp.)
abstract: An upper bound on the first-event error probability for maximum-likelihood decoding of fixed binary convolutional codes on the binary symmetric channel is derived. The bound is evaluated for rate<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</tex>codes, and comparisons are made with simulations and with the bounds of Viterbi, Van de Meeberg, and Post. In particular, the new bound is significantly better than Van de Meeberg's bound for rates above<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R_{\comp}</tex>.

articleTitle: Optimum waveform signal sets with amplitude and energy constraints
abstract: It is desirable to choose the waveforms making up a signaling alphabet so that they are maximally separated one from another. This problem is considered, in the space of square-integrable functions, for signals which have finite duration, and are constrained in the ranges of their values as well as in energy. Corresponding to each of the following cases, we establish sharp bounds for the minimum distance and for the average distance between elements of a fixed size signal set, and construct sets of signals that attain both bounds simultaneously. \begin{list} \item {\em Case A (Energy Constraint Only):} The average energy of the waveforms in the signal set is at most<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\sigma</tex>, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0 \leq \sigma < \infty</tex>. \item {\em Case B (Energy and Peak Amplitude Constraints):} The average energy of the waveforms in the signal set is<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\leq \sigma (0 \leq \sigma < 1)</tex>, and the absolute value of each waveform is at most<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</tex>. \item {\em Case C (Energy and Value Constraints):} The average energy of the waveforms in the signal set is at most<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b^{2}\sigma + a^{2}(1 - \sigma)</tex>, and each waveform takes values in the set<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[a, b]</tex>, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0 \leq a < b < \infty</tex>, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0 \leq \sigma \leq 1</tex>. \end{list} Cases A and B are applicable to signal design for communication in channels with additive noise (say Gaussian), and Case C is applicable to signal design for optical channels, where the signal represents the intensity of a photon stream. The general character of the results is that the minimum distance behaves like<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\gamma \sigma</tex>in Cases A and B, and like<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\gamma \sigma (1 - \sigma)</tex>in Case C, with<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\gamma</tex>a suitable constant.

articleTitle: Poor error correction codes are poor error detection codes (Corresp.)
abstract: We show that binary group codes that do not satisfy the asymptotic Varshamov-Gilbert bound have an undesirable characteristic when used as error detection codes for transmission over the binary symmetric channel.

articleTitle: Fast progressive reconstruction of a transformed image (Corresp.)
abstract: Fast methods for performing progressive reconstruction of Fourier and Hadamard transformed images have been developed. Reconstruction of an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N \times N</tex>point transformed image can be evaluated in order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N^{2} \log_{2} N</tex>instructions. Accumulation of round-off errors due to iteration is reduced by the factor<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(\log_{2} N + 1) / N^{2}</tex>, compared with direct evaluation of the inverse transform.

articleTitle: Ramp crossings for Slepian's process (Corresp.)
abstract: An expression for the probability density on the unit interval of the time to first ramp crossing is derived for Slepian's process, a Gaussian process with a triangular correlation function.

articleTitle: The capacity of digital links in tandem
abstract: Suppose we have<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</tex>digital links in tandem. Between successive links we have a repeater. The links are each white Gaussian channels with no bandwidth constraint. The repeater may either be a {\em binary repeater}, which sends on each bit separately having made a binary decision on each, or a {\em Shannon repeater}, which perfectly reproduces at one end the bits that were transmitted at the other end of the link. What is the loss in capacity if we use only binary repeaters and code for the entire L links at the transmit end? For large<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</tex>, the capacity drops by a factor asymptotic to In<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</tex>, and the normalized optimum time<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</tex>per symbol<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T_{\opt}^{L}</tex>is also asymptotic to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\ln L</tex>. Arbitrarily short<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</tex>gives<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</tex>capacity for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L > 1</tex>. More precise asymptotic results are obtained and compared with computed numerical values. These results show when it pays to code each link separately in digital data transmission.

articleTitle: Multidimensional digitization of data followed by a mapping (Corresp.)
abstract: In many applications it is necessary to digitize data, knowing only that later on some random function of the digitized data will be of interest. This problem is investigated when the data digitizers are allowed to be multidimensional, i.e., they map a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</tex>-dimensional data vector into one of a set of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</tex>-dimensional output vectors. It is shown that very complex distortion measures arise naturally. Results are given for the error measure defined as the squared value of the difference between the function of the digitized data and the function of the undigitized data.

articleTitle: An error-trapping decoder for nonbinary cyclic codes (Corresp.)
abstract: The error-trapping decoder is the simplest way of decoding cyclic codes satisfying<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R < 1 / t</tex>, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</tex>is the maximum number of errors to be corrected and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</tex>is the code rate. These codes have low rates and/or correct only a few errors. Kasami has used the concept of covering polynomials to demonstrate modified error-trapping decoders for several binary cyclic codes not satisfying<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R<1/t</tex>. In this paper Kasami's decoder is modified further for correcting multiple symbol errors on nonbinary cyclic codes satisfying<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R < 2 / t</tex>. The Berlekamp decoder for these codes requires Galois field multiplication and division of two variables which are difficult to implement. Our decoder does not require these multiplications and divisions. Further, for all double-error-correcting codes, and triple-error-correcting codes with rate<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R < 2/3</tex>, an algorithm is presented for finding a minimum set of covering monomials.

articleTitle: Maximum entropy spectral analysis and ARMA processes (Corresp.)
abstract: The maximum entropy spectral analysis for discrete-time stationary processes was first proposed by J. P. Burg. He showed that if a finite number of covariance lag values of a stationary process are known, then an autoregressive (AR) process with the given autocorrelation values best fits the given constraints in the sense of maximizing thc differential entropy rate of the model. A more general type of prior knowledge of the process is considered, and it is shown that the maximum entropy method, subject to our constraints, is equivalent to fitting a mixed autoregressive moving average (ARMA) model.

articleTitle: Predictive source coding techniques using maximum likelihood prediction for compression of digitized images
abstract: A predictive compression technique is examined, using maximum likelihood prediction of the image pixel based on the Markov mesh model, that encodes the differences via Gordon block-bit-plane (GBBP) encoding. The procedure is very efficient in that it requires a bit rate near the entropy of the source. For images with many quantization levels, maximum likelihood prediction can be cumbersome to implement. Thus, a suboptimal procedure called differential bit-plane coding (DBPC) is investigated. This is easily implemented, even for a large number of quantization levels, and is reasonably efficient.

articleTitle: The probability of undetected error when a code is used for error correction and detection (Corresp.)
abstract: We study the probability of having an undetected error when a linear block code is used to correct up to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</tex>errors on a symmetric channel, and the remaining power of the code is used for error detection.

articleTitle: Further classifications of codes meeting the Griesmer bound (Corresp.)
abstract: For any<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(n, k, d)</tex>binary linear code, the Griesmer bound says that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n \geq \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \lceil d/2^{i} \rceil</tex>, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\lceil x \rceil</tex>denotes the smallest integer<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\geq x</tex>. We consider codes meeting the Griesmer bound with equality. These codes have parameters<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">left( s(2^{k} - 1) - \sum_{i=1}^{p} (2^{u_{i}} - 1), k, s2^{k-1} - \sum_{i=1}^{p} 2^{u_{i} -1} \right)</tex>, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k > u_{1} > \cdots > u_{p} \geq 1</tex>. We characterize all such codes when<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p = 2</tex>or<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u_{i-1}-u_{i} \geq 2</tex>for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2 \leq i \leq p</tex>.

articleTitle: Notes on the asymptotic behavior of the information rate of block codes (Corresp.)
abstract: The behavior of the signaling rate of error-correcting codes of length<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>and minimum distance<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d_{n}</tex>is studied in the limit for large<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>when the sequence<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d_{n}/n</tex>approaches a prescribed limit<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\delta</tex>. A function<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R(\delta)</tex>representating the asymptotic signaling rate is defined and is shown to be continuous.

articleTitle: Shape and duration of clicks in modulated FM transmission
abstract: A Slepian model is derived for the shape of dicks in modulated FM transmission. The modulated signal may be a deterministic periodic function or a stationary stochastic process, not necessarily Gaussian. To describe the clicks one first derives the stochastic properties of noise and signal at the clicks. (For a periodic signal this amounts to giving the relative number of clicks in any given part of the period.) Then the conditional distributions of noise and signal near clicks are derived in explicit form, using the noise and signal values at the click as (random) parameters, and finally these conditional distributions are mixed into a total model for the click shapes. For increasing carrier-to-noise power ratio<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A^{2}/2</tex>, the Slepian model converges after normalization to a rational function with random coefficients. The amplitude of a click is shown to be of the order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A^{2}</tex>, in contrast to the unmodulated ease, where click amplitudes are of the order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</tex>.

articleTitle: Some new bounds for the maximum length of circuit codes (Corresp.)
abstract: A<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</tex>-dimensional circuit code of spread<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</tex>is a simple circuit<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</tex>in the graph of the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</tex>-dimensional unit cube with the property that for any vertices<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</tex>of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</tex>that differ in exactly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</tex>coordinates<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r < s</tex>, there exists a path from<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</tex>to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</tex>consisting of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</tex>edges of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</tex>. Some new lower bounds will be given for the maximum length of a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</tex>-dimensional circuit code of spread<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</tex>for some values of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</tex>and for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s = 4, s = 6</tex>, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s = 7</tex>.

articleTitle: The2rth mean convergence of adaptive filters with stationary dependent random variables
abstract: The<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</tex>th mean convergence of an adaptive filtering algorithm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C_{n+ 1} = C_{n} - a_{n}(C_{n}^{T} X_{n} - \alpha_{n}) X_{n}</tex>is studied, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\alpha_{n}</tex>'s and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X_{n}</tex>'s are useful random signals and observation vectors, respectively, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\{ a_{n} \}</tex>is a sequence of positive numbers decreasing to zero. In this work, we suppose that the sequence<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\{(\alpha_{n},X_{n})\}</tex>is a stationary mixing sequence (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\rho</tex>-mixing,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\phi</tex>-mixing, or<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\psi</tex>-mixing). Under some additional conditions it is shown that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C_{n}</tex>converges to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c_{\ast}</tex>in the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</tex>th mean, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c_{\ast}</tex>is the unique solution of the Wiener-Hopf equation.

articleTitle: Using codes for error correction and detection (Corresp.)
abstract: A linear code<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</tex>over GF<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(q)</tex>is good for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</tex>-error-correction and error detection if<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P(C,t;\epsilon) \leq P(C,t;(q - 1)/q)</tex>for all<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\epsilon, 0 \leq \epsilon \leq (q - 1)/q</tex>, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P(C, t; \epsilon)</tex>is the probability of an undetected error after a codeword in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</tex>is transmitted over a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</tex>-ary symmetric channel with error probability<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\epsilon</tex>and correction is performed for all error patterns with<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</tex>or fewer errors. A sufficient condition for a code to be good is derived. This sufficient condition is easy to check, and examples to illustrate the method are given.

articleTitle: An Upper Bound on the Key Equivocation for Pure Ciphers
abstract: An upper bound on key equivocation for a pure cipher applied on a memoryless message source is derived.

articleTitle: Robust Wiener filtering for multiple inputs with channel distortion (Corresp.)
abstract: Robust Wiener filtering has previously been considered for the single-input (scalar) case where there is no channel distortion and where the signal to be estimated is the source signal itself. Here, these results are extended to the multiple-input (vector) case where linear channel distortion is allowed and the signal to be estimated is a linear-filtered version of the source signal. The results are obtained from those for the single-input ease by modifying the constraints on signal and noise characteristics. Such a modification is motivated by examining the expression of the mean-squared error for the optimum filter.

articleTitle: Probability of error for digital systems with inaccurately known interference (Corresp.)
abstract: The "moment bound theory" is known to provide a useful technique to evaluate error probabilities for digital communication systems in the presence of additive noise and random interference. In this correspondence this theory is extended to the case where the moments of the interference are known only within certain intervals, and upper and lower bounds to the error probabilities are sought. A situation like this can occur in several applications. For example, the exact statistics of the interference may not be known, and only estimates of the first moments may be available. Another example arises when the signal is disturbed by intersymbol interference generated by a channel impulse response whose samples are known only in a certain interval--either because they have been measured with finite accuracy, or because we want to estimate the error probability for a class of channel impulse responses. Several numerical examples are provided which show the range of applicability of this technique.

articleTitle: Analysis of a new nonlinear filter and tracking methodology (Corresp.)
abstract: A recursive nonlinear filter and tracking methodology is developed for a class of partially observable processes with an approximating model which is linear in the unobservable states and initially has the unobservables conditionally Gaussian with respect to the observations. The usual model smoothness is not required, and applications to simulated tracking problems show the filter to be considerably more accurate than the modified second-order filter which in a general sense includes the extended Kalman filter.

articleTitle: A remark on radar ambiguity functions (Corresp.)
abstract: The ambiguity function of a signal<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f(t)</tex>determines<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</tex>up to a constant. Here we explore the extent to which<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</tex>can be modified without affecting the modulus of its ambiguity function.

articleTitle: Improvements of Winograd's result on computation in the presence of noise (Corresp.)
abstract: Winograd's result concerning Elias' model of computation in the presence of noise can be stated without reference to computation. If a code<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\varphi: \{0,1\}^{k} \rightarrow \{0,1\}^{n}</tex>is min-preserving<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(\varphi (a \wedge b) = \varphi (a) \wedge \varphi (b)</tex>for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a,b \in \{0,1\}^{k})</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\epsilon n</tex>-error correcting, then the rate<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k/n \rightarrow 0</tex>as<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k \rightarrow \infty</tex>. This result is improved and extended in two directions. \begin{enumerate} \item For min-preserving codes with {\em fixed} maximal (and also average) error probability on a binary symmetric channel again<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k/n \rightarrow 0</tex>as<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k \rightarrow \infty</tex>(strong converses). \item Second, codes with lattice properties without reference to computing are studied for their own sake. Already for monotone codes<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">( \varphi (a) \leq \varphi (b)</tex>for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a \leq b)</tex>the results in direction 1) hold for maximal errors. \end{enumerate} These results provide examples of coding theorems in which entropy plays no role, and they can be reconsidered from the viewpoint of multiuser information theory.

articleTitle: On an infinite series of[4n, 2n]binary codes (Corresp.)
abstract: This correspondence deals with an infinite series of binary, reversible<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[4n, 2n, 4], n \geq 2</tex>, unequal error protection codes, which are majority logic decodable. The weight enumerators and automorphism groups are determined completely. For n even the codes are self dual. By pasting together copies of a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[4n,2n,4]</tex>code, binary codes with parameters<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[8n,2n,8]</tex>for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n \geq 2, [8n,2n,12]</tex>for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n \geq 4</tex>, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[12n,2n,16]</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[16n,2n,24]</tex>for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n \geq 3</tex>are obtained.

articleTitle: Comments on "On a direct method of analysis and synthesis of the SPRT" by I. Vrana
abstract: In this brief communication, some comments on the above paper are made. The efficiency of the method of analysis proposed by Vrana and other methods available in literature are compared.

articleTitle: Generalizations of the Korzhik bound (Corresp.)
abstract: The probability of undetected error is studied when a code is used both for error correction and error detection. A number of generalizations is given of an upper bound of Korzhik on the minimal probability of undetected error for an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(n, k)</tex>code.

articleTitle: Upper bounds and construction techniques for signal sets with constrained synchronous correlation and specified time - bandwidth product (Corresp.)
abstract: Upper bounds are presented on the size of equal energy continuous time signal sets occupying a given time-bandwidth (TB) product under specified synchronous correlation constraints. Both time-limited (aperiodic) and periodic signal sets are addressed, with appropriate measures of bandwidth for each. Signal set construction techniques are derived which illustrate that the bounds for periodic signal sets are relatively tight, while those obtained for aperiodic signal sets are tight under certain conditions.

articleTitle: The continued fraction as an information source (Corresp.)
abstract: Nearly every digit (positive-integer partial quotient) of the simple continued fraction representing a random number carries<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.4325</tex>bits of information about the number. This is reduced by 0.0081 bit if the preceding digit is already known and by a further<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.0007</tex>bit if the second preceding digit is also known, Any finite sequence of digits is equally likely to occur forward and backward. Hence, the digit (source output symbol) following any digit likewise gives<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.0081</tex>bit of information about the latter, and all succeeding (or preceding) digits together give<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.0088</tex>bit despite the unbounded range of the statistical dependence among digits.

articleTitle: The minimum distance of the [38,19] ternary extended QR-code is 11 (Corresp.)
